In Uptown, its share of the houses listed in New Westminster went from 6.4% in June to 9.3% in October and its share of the condos and townhomes listed went from 22.3% to 23.5%. A share that holds steady while the city moves means the community is following the city; a share that drifts means it is moving differently.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Uptown NW
Fee-simple lots

items.t: The residential side streets off the Sixth Street core are single-detached homes under the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 — a mix of the city's older housing stock and later infill. RS-1 (s.310) sets a minimum site area of 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5. Freehold dominates the side streets: a fee-simple Uptown lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees — title, City bylaws and any registered covenants govern.

Added-homes potential is part of the lot's value: the RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway / carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw — a standard check on any Uptown house purchase, and documented, permitted suite space is a marketable feature on resale.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Uptown NW

items.t: What and where: Uptown is the City of New Westminster's uphill commercial and civic core, centred on Sixth Street and Sixth Avenue above the Downtown waterfront — roughly between Royal Avenue / Sixth Avenue, Eighth Street and Tenth Street, taking in City Hall (511 Royal Avenue), the New Westminster Public Library Main Branch (716 6th Avenue), Moody Park's east edge and the Sixth Street shopping corridor.

Nearby areas: Downtown and the Quay below the hill to the south, Queen's Park to the east, Brow of the Hill to the west, Moody Park and Glenbrooke North to the north, The Heights beyond McBride Boulevard.

Planning identity: Uptown is identified in the City's Official Community Plan — Our City 2041, Bylaw No. 7925, 2017 — as a Frequent Transit Development Area, one of the areas where the City directs higher-density, transit-supportive growth. That is a planning direction for the core, not a rezoning of any specific lot.

Schools (SD40; Ministry-listed names only; catchments are address-based): two completed School Locator runs are documented in this area's own research (SD40 School Locator, run 2026-10-21), each on a single-address basis — 835 Eighth Street (east side) → Lord Kelvin Elementary, Fraser River Middle, New Westminster Secondary; 1714 Eighth Avenue (west side) → École Lord Tweedsmuir Elementary, Fraser River Middle, New Westminster Secondary, with Early French Immersion at Lord Tweedsmuir itself. SD40 operates only one secondary school; the replacement New Westminster Secondary School at 820 Sixth Street opened January 11, 2021 ($106.5 million, 1,900 seats) and is already operating above capacity per the district's long-range facilities plan. Catchments for other Uptown addresses: Not verified.

Transit and roads: there is no SkyTrain station inside Uptown; the nearest are New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) at the foot of the hill downtown. TransLink routes 105 (Uptown / New Westminster Station) and 106 (Edmonds Station / New Westminster Station) run through the Uptown corridors, and routes 103 and 123 also serve the Sixth Street / Sixth Avenue area. Sixth Street, Sixth Avenue, Eighth Street and Royal Avenue are the main streets; McBride Boulevard links the area north to Sapperton and south toward the Pattullo Bridge. Driving commute times: Not verified — no official source publishes them.

Shopping and civic anchors: Royal City Centre, the enclosed mall at 610 Sixth Street, describes itself as New Westminster's premier shopping destination with over 40 shops and services (mall operator source: the Sixth Street and Sixth Avenue street-front corridors carry the rest of Uptown's shops, restaurants and services. Recreation: Moody Park (outdoor pool, spray park, sports fields; Moody Park Arena at 701 8th Avenue) and, a short distance east, the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue, fully opened May 2024. The city's hospital is Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street in Sapperton.

Flood position — this area's own, stated precisely: the City's floodplain study zones only the low-lying edges — Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 west-end Fraser River industrial land, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront and Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area. No floodplain zone for the Uptown plateau was confirmed on a City source; no zone is imported from any other sub-area, and lot-level status is checked with the City.
ALR: no Agricultural Land Reserve land is identified in Uptown; ALR status for any specific property is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Population context: the 2021 Census counted 78,916 people in New Westminster, up 11.2% from 70,996 in 2016, at 5,052 people per sq. km — the second-densest municipality in Canada. An Uptown-only population figure is not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Uptown NW

items.t: City plans and zoning (New Westminster's own bylaws): OCP "Our City 2041," Bylaw No. 7925, 2017; Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001. Apartment buildings concentrate along the Sixth Street / Sixth Avenue core under the multiple-unit residential and commercial high-rise districts; the side streets sit in the RS districts — RS-1 (s.310): minimum site area 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR 0.5. Secondary suites are allowed in the RS districts and laneway / carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw.
Heritage: Uptown's side streets hold some of the city's older housing stock.
Purchase prohibition / speculation taxes: Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax (3%) does NOT apply — it is a City of Vancouver tax only.

blocks.text: Good to know about Uptown NW

items.t: Uptown's attached depth is apartments, not lots.

One street, three buildings, one name trap: on Queens Avenue, the non-profit seniors rental Hillside Place (1025) faces the general-market strata tower Amara Terrace (1026) across the street, with Queens Terrace (1032) on the same block — and a second Hillside Place (509 Carnarvon Street, Downtown NW) is a market strata. Only the street address is a safe identifier.

The city's only secondary school is already over capacity. New Westminster Secondary (820 Sixth Street, 1,900 seats, opened January 11, 2021) is above capacity in SD40's own long-range facilities plan — it matters to every Uptown family purchase regardless of elementary catchment.

One Uptown tower opens into the mall — and its directory record is stale. The Woodward (612 Sixth Street, LMS3871) has direct internal access to Royal City Centre per its manager's welcome package, but its directory record still prints a "rentals not allowed" line voided November 24, 2022, and its unit count conflicts across sources (Not confirmed).

Legion Manor's published counts are from 2009. Every published figure for Legion Manor (123 + 6 accessible units) traces to the City's 2009 Non-Market Housing Inventory; the current count is not confirmed.

Approved claims, where a future page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

blocks.text: Uptown home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

125 condos sold in Uptown with a median price of $529,000 (the middle half sold between $405,000 and $627,500), taking a median of 25 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $548 per square foot, a median year built of 1992 and a median strata fee of $572 a month. 10 houses sold in Uptown with a median price of $1,312,500 (the middle half sold between $1,143,750 and $1,537,500), taking a median of 16 days to sell at 98.2% of the last list price; 10% sold above list. They had a median $601 per square foot, a median year built of 1927 and a median lot of 4,458 square feet.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Uptown?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 14 houses and 97 condos and townhomes listed in Uptown. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Uptown a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 7% (a buyers’ market); condos and townhomes had 24% (a sellers’ market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Uptown from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses and 81 condos and townhomes sold in Uptown over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in June with 1 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in October with 23 sold.

faq.q: How big is Uptown compared with the rest of New Westminster?
faq.a: In October 2026, Uptown held 9.3% of the 151 detached houses listed in New Westminster and 23.5% of the 413 condos and townhomes listed in New Westminster.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Uptown?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 12.6% of the 111 homes listed in Uptown and condos and townhomes made up 87.4%; of the 24 that sold, houses were 4.2% and condos and townhomes 95.8%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Uptown than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses rose from 10 in June to 14 in October 2026 (+40.0%); condos and townhomes fell from 106 in June to 97 in October 2026 (−8.5%).

faq.q: Is there a bare-land subdivision or a lot package I can buy in Uptown?
faq.a: Uptown is a built-out plateau — what trades as land is the individual fee-simple RS house lot (RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq.

faq.q: Is any Uptown lot a bare-land strata lot?
faq.a: None verified. If a listing suggests strata tenure on a detached-looking lot, tenure is a title check: a bare-land strata lot carries a Form B, strata fees and registered bylaws even though the house on it looks freehold.

faq.q: What does the Frequent Transit Development Area label mean for my lot?
faq.a: It is a planning direction in Our City 2041 (Bylaw 7925, 2017) steering higher-density, transit-supportive growth to the Sixth Street / Sixth Avenue core — not a rezoning of your lot. Confirm the exact designation and zoning with the City before pricing in redevelopment value.

faq.q: RT-A / RT-B — is that Uptown townhouse zoning?
faq.a: No. Those districts do not exist in Bylaw No. 6680; the townhouse districts are RT-2–RT-2C + RT-3/3A/3B.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or a laneway house to an Uptown lot?
faq.a: The RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway / carriage houses are regulated under Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 — pull the City permits and confirm the specific lot's permissions before valuing the second dwelling; documented, permitted suite space is a marketable feature on resale.

faq.q: I read that Uptown townhouses sit in "RT-A and RT-B" districts — is that right?
faq.a: No. RT-A and RT-B do not exist in New Westminster; the townhouse districts in Zoning Bylaw 6680 (2001) are RT-2–RT-2C and RT-3/3A/3B. And 836.10 m² is an RM apartment-district density threshold, not a townhouse minimum.

faq.q: Is Penny Lane a half duplex I can buy one side of?
faq.a: A strata unit there is bought as a strata lot under Form B diligence — it is not a duplex half in either legal form documented here.

faq.q: Can an Uptown house carry a suite or a laneway house?
faq.a: The RS districts allow secondary suites and regulate laneway / carriage houses under Zoning Bylaw 6680 — pull the City permits before advertising suite space, and note a suite is not a separately saleable half.

faq.q: What did condos in Uptown sell for?
faq.a: 125 condos sold in Uptown between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $529,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Uptown?
faq.a: The median was 25 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.0% of the last list price (6% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
